As your plane travels through the sky, the drag force caused by air resistance slows it down. You\novercome the effect of this force by adding thrust - "moar engines" - or improving aero shape.

Drag is the force that's slowing you down.

more drag usually means less speed and 
therefore less lift.

Jet Engines provide the thrust for our aircraft. These engines use intakes to get their oxygen. This means \nyou don't have to carry oxidizer along, but you can only operate where the atmosphere is thick enough.
If you are trying to build a Single Stage to Orbit (SSTO) craft then you might use jet engines to ascend to \nthe upper atmosphere and then use rockets to push from there to orbit.
Your aircraft needs air intakes and liquid fuel to feed the jet engine.

While all intakes perform the same function, you will find that some are better suited to your design, \nvisually or functionally. It's important to pick the right part for the job, and pay attention to the specs \nwhen building.
Intakes, like engines, come in many shapes and sizes. The key thing to remember is that they grab air \nfor jet engines, and the amount varies depending on speed and altitude.
The faster you go, the more air is captured; the higher \nyou go, the less air is captured (because the atmosphere \nis thinner at higher altitudes).
